## 假日固定收益簡報

### 美伊和平談判延期，美國債市適逢六月節休市

美國固定收益市場週五因六月節休市，沒有當日美債收盤價可供比較。當天最重要的新消息是，原定週五舉行、攸關美伊永久和平協議的談判延期。雙方能否達成持久安排、荷姆茲海峽能否穩定通行，因此仍有變數。

臨時協議已讓油輪開始通過海峽，確實朝供應恢復跨出一步；談判延期沒有抹去這項進展，卻使航運、能源與運費仍暴露於再次受阻的風險。Fed主席Kevin Warsh首次主持會議後，官員上修通膨預測，市場也已完整反映10月前升息1碼。下一項能檢驗能源衝擊是否擴散至其他物價的美國數據，是6月25日公布的5月PCE物價；市場預估整體月增0.5%、核心月增0.3%。

在美債休市期間，外匯與黃金市場仍持續調整Fed前景。面額至少€2億、約合$2.29億的歐元兌美元買權，成交量接近同類賣權的2倍；彭博美元現貨指數則朝單週上漲1%邁進。高盛因不再預期2026年降息，將年底黃金目標價下調$500至$4,900；在其升息情境下，金價估計為$4,400。這些是選擇權交易與機構預測，並非6月19日的美債價格反應。

## 全球利率、信用與主權發展

### 英國借款超出預期，公債殖利率走高

英國10年期公債殖利率上升5個基點至4.81%，表現落後歐洲同業。Andy Burnham在Makerfield勝選，提高其挑戰首相Keir Starmer的可能性，投資人因而重新檢視英國財政規則的穩定性。Burnham承諾維持現有框架，但部分顧問主張延長衡量期間、增加投資借款。現行債務規則已修訂過1次，5年內最多增加£700億借款空間；OECD預測2027年公共債務將達GDP的105.4%。

更直接的壓力來自財政數據。英國5月公共部門借款達£233億，較一年前多£54億，也高於預算責任辦公室（OBR）預測£56億。會計年度前2個月累計借款£463億，比OBR路徑高£77億。零售物價通膨推升通膨連動公債利息，5月債務利息支出增加£41億至創紀錄的£117億。不論未來由誰執政，這些數字都縮小了無財源支應新政策的空間。

家庭支出仍有韌性。5月零售銷量月增1.2%、年增3.2%，4月則修正為下降1.0%；3個月銷量增長0.4%，非實體通路大增6.1%。反彈承接疲弱的4月，且部分集中在網購，尚不能視為全面加速；但英國央行週四才有2位官員主張立即升息，這份數據也沒有提供需求急速降溫的新證據。

德國生產者物價顯示歐元區成本仍在上升。5月月增0.3%、年增2.2%，年增幅高於4月的1.7%；扣除能源後月增0.7%、年增2.3%，中間財年增4.2%。ECB首席經濟學家Philip Lane為近期將存款利率升至2.25%辯護，認為累積的成本壓力可能使通膨在2026年剩餘時間高於3%。他將中性利率估計上緣置於約2.5%，意味再升息一次，也未必使政策明顯轉為緊縮。

### 私募市場壓力，從債權條款延伸到抵押權

過去3年，至少€50億德國Schuldschein債權進入困境，對照這類工具每年約€200億的發行量，規模已不小。每筆債權可以切成€50萬，分散給數百家銀行與退休基金，但修改條款一般須所有債權人同意。BayWa重整涉及逾250名債權人。交易不活絡、缺少統籌債權人的受託機構，加上少數持有人拒絕妥協就可能引發交叉違約，使原本被視為穩健的德國企業融資，在出問題後尤其難協商。

英國央行另為私人市場設計壓力測試。嚴重但假設性的5年情境，包括利率達7%、英國股市下跌35%、槓桿貸款利差擴大400個基點、波動率指數達40，以及AI技術變化推升能源與硬體成本。銀行、機構投資人與BlackRock、Legal & General、Fidelity等管理業者參與。央行計畫只公布整體結果，不點名個別公司；情境描繪的是可能發生的系統衝擊，並不代表參與機構目前已經出問題。

Market Financial Solutions倒閉案的法院文件，則提出更具體的資產問題。某關係企業持有約£3億、約合$3.96億抵押貸款，但文件顯示這些抵押權似乎沒有完成登記，儘管相關融資原本是為短期房地產貸款提供資金。指控仍待司法程序釐清；若確實未登記，即使房地產本身有價值，證明抵押品所有權與回收資金也可能變得困難。

歐洲軟體貸款仍有選擇性買盤。AutoForm的€6.72億、約$7.7億定期貸款，約30%投資人拒絕展期，CLO則承接缺口，使到期日由2029年延至2032年；歐洲需求改善也讓定價收斂。AI帶動軟體業賣壓後，這筆交易顯示市場仍能找到支持者，但部分大型投資人拒絕展期，也說明大家對長期業務風險看法不同。

### 日本、印度與加拿大各有政策訊號

日本央行副總裁Ryozo Himino警告，企業之間的成本轉嫁加快，可能進一步推升消費物價，使基礎通膨超過2%目標。5月企業投入價格年增6.3%，為3年來最快。能源補貼壓低最新消費物價讀數，但服務與加工食品成本仍偏高。Himino認為，日圓偏弱增加通膨壓力；若延誤必要調整，未來可能被迫升息得更急。他的談話接續本週日本央行升至1%的決定。

央行理事會的人事變動，則可能使後續路徑更難預測。Toichiro Asada反對本週升息，現任鷹派委員任期屆滿後，政府的新任命也可能改變力量對比。調查顯示，市場對下次升息時間主要集中在10月與12月；委員之間仍有分歧，因此工資、服務價格與日圓走勢，比單靠日曆推估更重要。

日本3個月國庫券標售，在¥9兆6,375億競爭性投標中，接受¥3兆1,503.8億；加權平均殖利率0.9107%，最低得標價格對應殖利率0.9224%，均低於6月12日標售。另一筆針對剩餘5至11年天期債券的流動性增強操作，接受¥6,489億，平均利差為參考利率加0.016%。這些是日本當日標售與操作結果，國庫券於6月22日發行，並非美國休市期間的美債走勢。

加拿大4月名目零售銷售月增0.5%至C$730億，略低於預估0.6%，也慢於3月的0.9%。銷售量持平，扣除燃料與汽車的核心指標下降0.7%；加油站與汽車經銷商貢獻了大部分整體增幅。5月初步指標預示成長1.0%，但僅有52.1%的受訪企業提供回覆。接下來的通膨數據將有助加拿大央行判斷，零售金額上升究竟來自漲價，還是實際需求增加。

印度銀行取得定向的美元融資管道。至少4家銀行計畫透過印度央行年費率1.5%的交換窗口，發行約$25億美元債，因為貸款成長快於存款。稅制調整與外資流入，已使本地5年期政府債殖利率下降逾30個基點至6.49%。不過，銀行體系盈餘資金預估將接近8兆盧比、約$850億；印度央行遠期部位到期，以及可能動用準備金或反向附買回操作，仍可能收回部分流動性。分析師預期殖利率在6.50%附近趨穩。

Jio Platforms提議將IPO所得的2,750億盧比、約$29億，用於償還旗下電信事業近$30億的美元及日圓債務；IPO與還款都尚未完成。俄羅斯則因盧布走強、5月通膨降至5.3%並創近3年最低，得以降息，但幅度小於市場預期。財政赤字擴大、戰時支出，以及2026年成長預測下修至0.4%，限制了進一步寬鬆的空間。

## 下一交易日觀察

### 下個交易日，債券供給與通膨數據接續登場

美債於6月22日恢復交易，財政部當天計畫標售$890億13週及$770億26週國庫券，兩筆均於6月25日交割。6月23日還有$690億2年期公債，24日$700億5年期，25日$440億7年期。Fed會議與休市之後，這將是市場對政策敏感天期需求的一次更大檢驗。

能源成本的傳導，會先在美國以外接受檢驗。中國6月22日公布貸款市場報價利率，預期1年與5年期維持3.00%及3.50%；加拿大同日公布5月CPI，預期整體通膨由2.8%升至3.0%。澳洲6月24日公布5月CPI，先前月增與年增讀數為0.4%及4.2%。美國6月25日的PCE報告，則能讓投資人把本地物價廣度與海外數據放在一起比較。

日本計畫6月23日標售約¥2.5兆5年期公債、25日續發約¥7,000億20年期公債。隨著日本央行逐步調整政策，標售將檢驗本地買盤。英國投資人則會關注公債走弱後，政黨領導權與財政規則是否提出具體方案。這兩個市場當天有實際交易，美債對假日消息的反應仍須等6月22日開市。

## Holiday Fixed-Income Brief

### Peace Talks Slip as US Bond Markets Close for Juneteenth

US fixed-income markets were closed Friday for Juneteenth. With no Treasury session to price, attention shifted to news that could shape the next open: permanent US-Iran peace talks scheduled for the day were postponed, leaving the timing of a durable settlement and dependable passage through the Strait of Hormuz uncertain.

Oil tankers had begun moving through the strait under the interim agreement, a real step toward restoring supply. The delay in talks did not undo that movement, but it left shipping, energy and freight costs exposed to further disruption. The distinction matters after Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh's first meeting, when officials raised their inflation forecasts and the market priced a full quarter-point increase by October. The next evidence on whether the energy shock is reaching broader prices comes with May PCE inflation on June 25; consensus estimates are 0.5% monthly headline and 0.3% core.

Currency and commodity markets were already adjusting to the more restrictive Fed outlook. Euro-dollar call options tied to contracts of at least €200 million, or $229 million, traded at nearly twice the volume of comparable puts. The Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index was headed for a 1% weekly gain. Goldman Sachs cut its year-end gold target by $500 to $4,900 after dropping its expectation of a 2026 rate cut; its scenario with a hike put gold at $4,400. These were option flows and forecasts during the closure, not a June 19 Treasury price reaction.

## Global Rates, Credit, And Sovereign Developments

### UK Borrowing Surprise Sends Gilts Lower

The UK's 10-year gilt yield rose 5 basis points to 4.81%, underperforming European peers. Andy Burnham's victory in Makerfield raised the possibility of a challenge to Prime Minister Keir Starmer, bringing the durability of Britain's fiscal rules back into focus. Burnham has pledged to keep the existing framework, although some advisers favor longer measurement periods and more borrowing for investment. The debt rule has already been revised once to allow as much as £70 billion of extra capacity over five years; the OECD projects public debt at 105.4% of GDP in 2027.

The fiscal numbers gave investors a more immediate concern. Britain borrowed £23.3 billion in May, £5.4 billion more than a year earlier and £5.6 billion above the Office for Budget Responsibility forecast. Borrowing in the first two months of the fiscal year reached £46.3 billion, £7.7 billion above the OBR path. Debt-interest costs rose £4.1 billion to a record £11.7 billion in May as higher retail-price inflation increased payments on index-linked gilts. The figures left less room for unfunded policy changes, regardless of who eventually leads the government.

Household demand also held up. Retail-sales volumes rose 1.2% in May and 3.2% from a year earlier, after April was revised to a 1.0% decline. Volumes gained 0.4% over three months, while non-store sales jumped 6.1%. The rebound followed a weak April and was concentrated partly in online shopping; it nevertheless offered the Bank of England little new evidence of a sharp demand slowdown after two officials had voted to raise rates at Thursday's meeting.

German producer prices pointed to continued cost pressure in the euro area. They increased 0.3% in May and 2.2% over a year, accelerating from April's 1.7% annual pace. Excluding energy, producer prices rose 0.7% monthly and 2.3% annually; intermediate goods were 4.2% dearer than a year earlier. ECB Chief Economist Philip Lane defended the recent increase in the deposit rate to 2.25%, saying accumulated costs could keep inflation above 3% for the rest of 2026. He placed the upper end of neutral-rate estimates near 2.5%, leaving room for another increase without necessarily making policy clearly restrictive.

### Private-Market Strains Show Up in Contracts and Collateral

At least €5 billion of German Schuldschein debt has entered distressed situations over three years, compared with about €20 billion of annual issuance. The loan notes can be split into €500,000 pieces among hundreds of banks and pension funds, while amendments generally require unanimous creditor consent. BayWa's restructuring involved more than 250 creditors. Thin trading, the absence of a coordinating trustee and the possibility of cross-defaults make a workout difficult when even a few holders refuse to agree.

The Bank of England set out a separate stress test for private markets. Its severe five-year scenario includes 7% rates, a 35% fall in UK equities, 400 basis points of leveraged-loan spread widening, volatility at 40, and AI disruption that raises energy and hardware costs. Banks, investors and managers including BlackRock, Legal & General and Fidelity are participating. The bank plans to publish aggregate results, rather than identifying individual firms. The exercise describes a hypothetical system shock, not a current failure at any participant.

Court filings in the collapse of Market Financial Solutions raised a more immediate question about assets. A related company held about £300 million, or $396 million, of mortgages that did not appear to have been registered, even though the funding was meant to finance short-term property loans. The allegations remain subject to legal proceedings. If the registrations are missing, proving ownership of collateral and recovering money could be difficult independently of what the properties are worth.

European software loans offered a more constructive, though selective, result. CLOs bought enough of AutoForm's €672 million, or $770 million, term loan to fill the gap after about 30% of investors declined to extend it. The maturity moved from 2029 to 2032, and stronger European demand allowed the price to tighten. The deal found sponsorship following the AI-driven software selloff, while the holdouts showed that investors still disagreed about the borrower's long-term risk.

### Japan, India and Canada Add Their Own Policy Signals

Bank of Japan Deputy Governor Ryozo Himino warned that faster cost increases between businesses could feed into consumer prices and lift underlying inflation above the 2% target. Corporate input prices rose 6.3% over a year in May, their fastest pace in three years. Energy subsidies restrained the latest consumer reading, but services and processed-food costs remained firm. Himino said a weaker currency added to inflation and that delaying necessary adjustments could force more abrupt tightening later. His comments followed the BOJ's increase to 1% earlier in the week.

The board's composition may complicate that path. Toichiro Asada dissented from the latest hike, and future government appointments could shift the balance as current hawks' terms end. Surveys clustered expectations for another increase around October or December. The disagreement makes incoming wage, services-price and yen data more useful than the calendar alone.

Japan's 3-month bill auction accepted ¥3,150.38 billion of competitive bids from ¥9,637.50 billion submitted. The weighted-average yield was 0.9107%, with 0.9224% at the lowest accepted price, both below the June 12 sale. A separate liquidity operation for bonds with five to 11 years remaining accepted ¥648.9 billion at an average spread of +0.016% to its reference rate. These are auction outcomes rather than a price signal for the closed US market; the bills issue June 22.

Canadian nominal retail sales rose 0.5% in April to C$73.0 billion, just below the 0.6% forecast and slower than March's 0.9% gain. Volumes were unchanged, while the core measure excluding fuel and autos fell 0.7%; gasoline sellers and car dealers supplied much of the headline increase. A preliminary May indicator suggested a 1.0% gain but drew responses from only 52.1% of the companies surveyed. The Bank of Canada's next inflation reading will help distinguish higher prices from stronger real demand.

Indian lenders found a targeted dollar-funding channel. At least four banks planned about $2.5 billion of issuance using a Reserve Bank of India swap window priced at 1.5% annually, after loan growth outpaced deposits. Domestic five-year government yields had fallen more than 30 basis points to 6.49% on tax changes and foreign inflows. Yet surplus bank cash was projected to approach 8 trillion rupees, or $85 billion, before RBI forward maturities or potential reserve and reverse-repo operations withdrew some liquidity. Analysts expected yields to stabilize near 6.50%.

Jio Platforms proposed using 275 billion rupees, or $2.9 billion, of IPO proceeds to repay almost $3 billion of its telecom unit's dollar- and yen-denominated debt. The IPO and repayment had not been completed. Russia, meanwhile, lowered its policy rate by less than expected as a firmer ruble and May inflation of 5.3%, the slowest in almost three years, allowed some easing. A widening fiscal deficit, wartime spending and a reduced 2026 growth forecast of 0.4% limited the scope for more.

## Next Open-Session Watch

### The Next Open Session Faces Supply and Inflation Data

US bond trading resumes June 22, when Treasury plans to sell $89 billion of 13-week and $77 billion of 26-week bills, both settling June 25. A $69 billion 2-year note auction follows June 23, then $70 billion of 5-year notes June 24 and $44 billion of 7-year notes June 25. The week brings a larger test of demand for policy-sensitive bonds after the Fed meeting and the holiday pause.

Energy pass-through will first be measured abroad. China's June 22 loan prime-rate fixing is expected to leave one- and five-year rates at 3.00% and 3.50%. Canada's May CPI is due the same day, with headline inflation expected to rise to 3.0% from 2.8%; Australia's May CPI follows June 24, after previous monthly and annual readings of 0.4% and 4.2%. The US PCE release on June 25 will then put domestic price breadth beside those overseas measures.

Japan plans to sell about ¥2,500 billion of five-year bonds June 23 and reopen about ¥700 billion of 20-year bonds June 25. Those auctions will test domestic demand as the BOJ continues normalization. In Britain, investors will look for concrete leadership and fiscal-rule proposals following the gilt selloff. Both markets have live price discovery; any US Treasury response will await the next open session.

overall_summary.headline: Peace talks are postponed; UK borrowing pushes gilts lower during US closure
overall_summary.session_narrative:
There was no June 19 US Treasury close. The main diplomatic update was a postponement of permanent US-Iran peace talks, although oil tankers had begun moving through Hormuz under the interim agreement. The next US price response will come when markets reopen June 22. Currency options and a stronger dollar already reflected the more restrictive Fed outlook during the closure.

UK gilts did trade. The 10-year yield rose 5 basis points to 4.81% after May borrowing reached £23.3 billion, £5.6 billion above the official forecast, and debt-interest costs hit a record £11.7 billion. Political questions following Andy Burnham's Makerfield victory added to scrutiny of the fiscal rules. German producer prices also accelerated, while German Schuldschein distress and a UK private-market stress exercise drew attention to credit documentation and collateral risk.

Japan's deputy central-bank governor warned that rising business costs could feed consumer inflation. Canadian retail volumes were flat despite a nominal increase, and Indian banks planned dollar issuance through an RBI swap facility. The next US session opens with a large bill calendar, followed by coupon auctions and the June 25 PCE inflation report.
